match.reason: The closest bank point, e-externality, covers externalities in general, including positive ones and the social optimum with welfare loss, which is broader and deeper than this Year 11 VCE point on climate change as a negative externality, and the other bank point is about physical climate impacts rather than externalities.

draft.title: Climate change as an economic issue
card: When a firm or household burns fossil fuels, it releases greenhouse gas emissions. These add to climate change, which harms other people, such as farmers hit by drought or families hit by floods.
The polluter does not pay for this harm. It is an external cost, so it falls on third parties and is not in the price of the good.
This makes emissions a negative externality. The social cost is higher than the private cost, so the market produces more of the polluting good than the social optimum.
Firms and buyers have no reason to count the external cost on their own. Markets alone do not fix the problem, so a government or a group of governments may need to act.
draft.remember: The polluter does not pay for the harm from emissions, so the market makes too much.

a.q: Why is climate change described as a market failure?
opts: Emissions harm others, but the polluter does not pay
Emissions are a private cost paid only by the polluter
Markets cannot produce goods that use fossil fuels
Firms who pollute always make a loss in the market
a.why: The harm from emissions falls on third parties, so it is an external cost left out of the price. Because the polluter ignores it, the market makes too much of the polluting good. The cost is not private, as the polluter does not bear it.
a.clue: Who pays for the harm caused by the emissions?

b.q: Dan runs a coal-fired power station in Victoria. His price covers fuel, wages and equipment, but not the harm from his emissions. What does this mean for his output?
opts: It is higher than the social optimum
It is lower than the social optimum
It equals the social optimum
It is zero, because the harm is a private cost
b.why: The harm from emissions is an external cost, so the price is based on private cost alone. Private cost is below social cost, so more is produced than the social optimum. The option saying output is lower reverses the effect, which belongs to positive externalities.
b.clue: Is the price based on private cost or social cost?

a.best: Emissions harm others, but the polluter does not pay

b.best: It is higher than the social optimum

a.q: Why do markets alone not fix the harm from emissions?
opts: Polluters do not pay for the harm their emissions cause
Polluters pay the full cost of emissions in their prices
The harm is a private cost paid only by the buyer
Markets make less of polluting goods than is best
a.why: The harm falls on third parties and is left out of the price, so firms and buyers have no reason to count it. It is not a private cost, because neither the buyer nor the seller bears it. That is why the market makes too much, not too little, of the polluting good.
